premises: Intrinsic reduction kinetics of noble metal precursors can be manipulated by modulating their instantaneous concentrations via precursor addition rate.
Synchronized reduction kinetics promote simultaneous nucleation and uniform atomic mixing, favoring single-phase solid-solution formation.
Uncontrolled or asynchronous reduction leads to phase separation, elemental segregation, and non-uniform structures.
The approach is effective for systems with more than five elements and significant differences in reduction potentials under rapid thermal cycling.
